ratingMethod.scale: 100 is the same-season subdivision reference. Ten points represent one adjusted yard-equivalent per attempt after shrinkage.

terms.Y: Passing yards in complete attributed rows
terms.D: Sum of attempts × opposing defense allowance for each game
terms.A: Pass attempts in complete attributed rows
terms.L: Attempt-weighted opponent-adjusted passing rate of covered same-season passers in the same subdivision

ratingMethod.opponentFormula: Defense allowance = (opponent prior yard-equivalents − prior subdivision rate × opponent prior attempts) / (opponent prior attempts + 180). Use evidence available at least 24 hours after earlier game kickoffs.
ratingMethod.explanation: Yards measure progress. Touchdowns earn 15 yard-equivalents and interceptions cost 40 as fixed experimental weights. Completion count checks the input and is visible alongside the rating. Sixty reference attempts pull a short record toward average. Earlier same-subdivision opponent samples measure passing defense before the game.
ratingMethod.limitation: The model uses passing box-score evidence. Published rushing yards can include sacks, and player fumble data does not consistently distinguish QB plays or assign lost fumbles. Rushing, sacks and fumbles remain separate evidence until their attribution can be verified. FBS and FCS use separate comparison groups.
